title: AltDigital Managed Platform — onboarding questionnaire
description: Structured form of design/onboarding-questionnaire.md, which is the INPUT to account vesting rather than a document that gets filed. Only [A] asked fields appear here. [D] derived fields are computed by scripts/derive-vesting.py from vesting/derivation-rules.yaml and are rejected if supplied, because a derived value that can be typed is a derived value that can be wrong. [P] placeholder fields are owned outside this process and are marked required-but-nullable so their absence is visible rather than assumed.

schema_version.description: Pinned. A questionnaire is an audit artifact re-reviewed on the triggers listed in the source document, so a record written today must still be readable when its schema has moved on.

partner.description: 1.0 — partner slug. Must already exist and be active in the registry; create-client-ou.sh blocks otherwise. 18 chars to fit the account alias budget.

client_slug.description: 1.1 — machine-safe client id used in account alias and root email.

application_code.description: 1.3 — 10 chars. Tighter than client because the email local part is capped at 64 octets by RFC 5321, which binds before the 63-char account alias.

service_model.description: 1.4 — drives patching ownership, SLA scope, DNS and certificate ownership.

partner_is_application_owner.description: 1.0b — if true the partner appears in two columns of the responsibility matrix, which needs saying out loud rather than inferring.

frameworks.description: 2.1 — drives conformance packs, retention floor and pen test cadence. 'none' must be alone; enforced in derive-vesting.py, since JSON Schema cannot express 'this value excludes all others' without oneOf gymnastics that obscure the rule.

non_us_data_subjects.description: 2.2 — asks about DATA SUBJECTS, not customer location. True HALTS vesting: region choice then carries a residency and transfer position that is a legal determination, and the platform's allowed regions are US-only.

data_classification.description: 2.3 — seeds the egress profile default and monitoring tier.

baa_window_partner_to_client_hours.description: 2.6 — marked [P] in the source: owned by Art and Wayne, not asked of the customer here. Nullable so an unanswered value is VISIBLE. Null blocks vesting where PHI is true; a missing key would let it pass unnoticed, which is the failure this nullability exists to prevent. AltDigital's own window (2.6a) is not here at all — it comes from the partner's registry record and must be strictly tighter.

egress_profile.description: 3.2 — the customer's answer overrides the classification-derived default. 'locked' is accepted here but NOT implemented (B-010); derive-vesting.py flags it rather than failing at the network step after three accounts exist.

inbound_cross_tenant_api.description: 3.4 — true is documented as an arm's-length public API. No private connectivity is provisioned between tenants, ever.

outbound_allowlist.description: 3.5 — domains for the Network Firewall or DNS Firewall rule set.

uat_required.description: 3a.1 — opt-in fourth account. Raises AWS cost.

release_cadence.description: 3a.2 — drives HOOP versus seasonal teardown. Required when uat_required is true; enforced in derive-vesting.py.

usage_pattern.description: 3a.3 — seasonal makes the account eligible for the dormant lifecycle.

timezone.description: 3a.7 — IANA name, e.g. America/Chicago. One timezone for all HOOPs.

uat.description: 3a.6 — saving here is modest; users test on their own schedule.

manual_turnup_authorised.description: 3a.8 — who may bring an environment up outside its HOOP. Empty means nobody can, which is a support call waiting to happen.

rpo_hours.description: 4.2 — default 2. Drives backup frequency and PITR.

backup_retention_days.description: 4.4 — null means the platform default applies.

maintenance_window.description: 4.5 — MUST fall inside the HOOP for scheduled environments. derive-vesting.py checks this: a maintenance window outside the HOOP means the instances are off when Patch Manager runs, so patching silently never happens and every report says compliant.

external_key_material.description: 5.3 — BYOK. Creates an EXTERNAL-origin key, which AWS cannot rotate and cannot recover if the customer loses the material.

no_regulated_data_in_lower_envs_ack.description: 5.7 — must be TRUE. Modelled as a const rather than a boolean because a questionnaire that records 'customer declined to acknowledge' and proceeds anyway is worse than one that cannot be submitted. If a customer will not acknowledge it, that is a scope conversation, not a field value.

dedicated_infrastructure_required.description: 5.9 — SECURITY-motivated, distinct from section 6 which is about LICENCES. Default false; docs/isolation-tiers.md carries the argument. Conflating the two produces a client paying a tenancy premium nobody can later explain.

dedicated_infrastructure_driver.description: 5.9a — determines whether it is negotiable. Required when 5.9 is true.

dedicated_infrastructure_control_ref.description: 5.9b — if a framework is cited, which control. Frameworks are cited far more often than read; none of HIPAA, PCI-DSS or SOC 2 requires dedicated physical hardware.

working_definition.description: 7.1 — 'what would a user notice first if it broke?' The source document calls this the only question a customer can genuinely fail to answer well, and it drives BOTH the canary and the SLA measurement. minLength is a blunt instrument against a one-word answer; it cannot detect a useless twenty-character one, and this remains a conversation rather than a form field.

acceptable_response_ms.description: 7.4 — canary timeout AND the SLA pass condition. One number, two consumers, deliberately.

existing_test_suite.description: 7.5 — decides Fargate canary runner versus native Synthetics.

cicd_tooling.description: 8.1 — OIDC federation for the AppDeployer role.

ip_boundary_ack.description: 9.1 — const for the same reason as 5.7.

post_exit_governance_loss_ack.description: 9.2 — the customer loses platform governance on exit. Acknowledged before vesting, not discovered at exit.

contact.description: Contacts are personal data. A completed questionnaire therefore must NEVER be committed — enforced in .gitignore and the pre-commit hook, the same treatment as config/contacts.env.

hoop.description: Hours of Planned Operation. always_on true ignores the rest; false requires days, start and end, enforced in derive-vesting.py because JSON Schema's if/then for this reads far worse than the check it replaces.
